title: observability: add token-level cost & latency metrics, tracing spans, dashboards, and alert tuning
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: customers and internal SREs have asked for better visibility into per-token cost and latency breakdowns (model, prefix vs generation, KV cache effects) to investigate regressions and tune routing/caching policies. This PR implements token-level metrics, improves tracing spans for generation and KV cache lookup, adds dashboard panels (Grafana) and updates alert thresholds to reduce noise while surfacing real regressions.

What this PR does (high level):
- Exposes new Prometheus metrics: redwood_token_cost_usd, redwood_token_latency_ms, redwood_token_count (labels: model, route, endpoint, customer_tier, kv_cache_hit)
- Adds KV cache-specific metrics and histograms: redwood_kv_lookup_latency_ms and redwood_kv_cache_hit_ratio
- Extends tracing: new spans for "kv_lookup", "kv_cache_hit", "generate_token" with tags for model, shard, and seq_len_bucket
- Dashboard: new Grafana dashboard (Observability > Token Cost & Latency) with per-model and per-route breakdowns, heatmaps for latency by seq_len, and cost leak detection panel
- Alert tuning: update alert rules to use token-rate-normalized thresholds (reduce noise for batchy traffic) and add runbook links for cost/latency incidents
- Tests & docs: unit tests for metric tagging, integration test that validates metrics emitted end-to-end, and docs/README for dashboards and how to interpret panels

Why: token-level metrics let platform and product teams quickly attribute cost spikes, detect regressions from model or quantization rollouts, and guide autoscaling and routing policies. Tracing improvements make it easier to correlate slow tokens with KV lookups and particular model shards.

Backward compatibility: metric names are additive and old collectors remain unchanged. Alerting logic is updated but defaults are conservative; customers can opt-out via config.

Release notes: Adds token-level cost & latency metrics, tracing spans for generation and KV lookups, a new Token Cost & Latency Grafana dashboard, and tuned alert rules to reduce false positives. See release notes section for migration/config tips.

review_comments: Aisha Patel: Nice work - I like the seq_len bucketing model. A couple of questions: how do we expect cardinality to behave with model+route+customer_tier labels? Can we avoid high-cardinality by sampling or coarse bucketing?

Maya Chen (author): We added coarse seq_len buckets (0-32,33-128,129-512,>512) and kv_cache_hit is boolean. For customer_tier we only emit for enterprise customers (config flag) to avoid cardinality explosion. Added note in README.
Ben Thompson: Alert tuning looks reasonable but we should test under synthetic load patterns (spikes + sustained growth). Did you run the canary workload against the new rules?
Maya Chen: Ran canary in staging for 48h; attached graphs in the PR. Adjusted thresholds to use 95th percentile over 30m window to reduce transient noise.
Diana Liu: One nit: use consistent metric units (ms for latency). Also please add a smoke test to CI that asserts metrics exist after start-up.
Maya Chen: Fixed units, added smoke test (ci/integration/token_metrics_smoke_test.sh), and ensured it runs in the integration pipeline.

manual_test_notes: Deployed to staging (region: us-west-2) and drove synthetic traffic using perf-canary with 3 model variants (redwood/gpt-neox-20b, redwood/llama-2-13b, open/phi-2).
Observed token-level cost panel reflect expected differences (quantized model lower cost), KV cache hit ratio correlated with reduced token latency in traces.
Validated runbook: followed steps in token_alerts.runbook.md to confirm alert routing and Slack paging behavior.

No breaking API changes. Defaults conservative; enterprise customers may opt-in to additional labels.
